summary: Klamath NF lookout on Craggy Peak; a 1960 CL-100 cab replaced an earlier pre-1939 cab; land-title dates conflict; in use in 2021.

facts.design: CL-100 all-steel cab on a 9-foot block tower (1960); earlier cab a Region 5 BC-302 design

access.note: Working fire-season station on Klamath National Forest land; no public visitor or rental listing found.

visit.drive_up: Reached by a good road from Callahan (2012 photo page)

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Earliest record I found of a lookout on the peak: F. J. Friday on leave from the Boliver lookout, Sept 1921 (Siskiyou Daily News, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Shasta Forest accepted title to the 20-acre site (May 12, 1936); lookout had been built on leased Southern Pacific land
NHLR says Southern Pacific deeded the property to the Forest Service in 1939; conflicts with the 1936 title date
Administration of the lookout taken over by the Klamath National Forest from the Shasta National Forest
Roof blown off the original structure (diary entry Sept 18, 1959); a temporary tent took its place
CL-100 all-steel cab on a 9-foot block tower replaced the previous structure; construction began late 1960; foundation forms carried up in October and floor slab poured in November
Date registered October 27, 2019 as NHLR US 1354, CA 177
Karita Knisely worked the tower May to October, four days a week, during the 2021 season

corrections.why: NHLR says the 1960 cab replaced an earlier structure, and a 1921 source already mentions a lookout on the peak

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says Southern Pacific deeded the property to the Forest Service in 1939; Forest Lookouts says the Shasta Forest accepted title to 20 acres in May 1936. The story reports both and does not choose.

sources.title: Fire lookouts keep watch over threatened forests

notes_for_editor: Brief status standing holds (NHLR 2019; staffed 2021). Brief access 'unknown' set to restricted. No height_m: NHLR gives only the 9-foot block tower, not total height. Peakbagging photo is dated July 2012. A 2021 River Complex (Haypress) fire link to this lookout appears only in social posts I could not open, so it is not in the story. Forest Fire Lookout Association list also shows it standing. Story is about 315 words after fact-check edits.
